channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks High in Digital Services and Child Rights Protection
item.description: Kazakhstan has achieved high positions in international rankings for digital public services and child rights protection, improving its scores in innovation and life satisfaction. The country ranked 34th out of 100 nations in the Most Powerful Countries 2026 index and 24th in the UN's 2024 e-government survey, showing significant progress.

item.title: Almaty's TETs-3 Modernization Delayed, New Power Capacity Lower Than Planned
item.description: The modernization of Almaty's TETs-3 power plant is behind schedule, with its launch now expected after 2026. Consequently, new power generation capacity in 2026 will be 1.27 GW, significantly less than the planned 2.66 GW. A gas power station in Turkestan also faces delays.

item.title: UN Envoy Highlights Grave Concerns Over Land Grabs and Forced Displacement of Hazaras
item.description: Afghanistan's UN envoy, Naseer Ahmad Faiq, expressed deep concern over land grabs, property confiscation, and the forced displacement of Hazara communities. He stated that the situation of ethnic and religious minorities under Taliban rule requires urgent attention, emphasizing that no citizen should face persecution based on ethnicity or religion.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Largest Gas Station Opens on Route to Charyn and Kaindy
item.description: Kusto Group has opened the Compass gas station in the Almaty region, representing Kazakhstan's largest such facility. With an investment of approximately 3 billion tenge, the station creates 80 jobs and is strategically located on the route to popular tourist destinations like Charyn Canyon and Kaindy Lake.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Consider Three-Year Moratorium on Small Business Inspections
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed relevant ministries to prepare proposals for a three-year moratorium on inspections of micro and small businesses, starting January 1, 2027. The goal is to reduce administrative burdens and minimize interference in business activities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes New Parliamentary Group "Children of Kazakhstan" for Rights Protection
item.description: A new parliamentary group named "Children of Kazakhstan" has been formed in the Kurultai, dedicated to protecting children's rights. Deputy Dana Medeuova will lead the group, which aims to focus on legislation concerning children's safety, health, and well-being. The group's formation was announced during an international forum on children's rights in Astana. Specific details on membership and legislative changes are yet to be announced.

item.title: Bishkek Court Begins Hearing Activist's Lawsuit for State Compensation in "Kempir-Abad Case"
item.description: The Pervomaysky District Court in Bishkek has started hearing a lawsuit filed by civil activist Perizat Suranova, who was previously accused and later acquitted in the "Kempir-Abad Case," seeking compensation from the state. The preliminary hearing took place on October 28, with the next session scheduled for November 10. A representative from the Ministry of Finance did not attend the initial hearing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Restricting Tap Water Use at Car Washes
item.description: Kazakhstan is planning to limit the use of centralized tap water for technical purposes at car washes. Amendments to the Water Code are being prepared to address this issue, as announced by the Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation, Nurzhan Nurzhigitov. This initiative is part of broader reforms in the water sector aimed at modernizing infrastructure and ensuring efficient water management.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government Outlines Post-Presidential Address Economic Measures
item.description: Kazakhstan's cabinet has detailed its post-Presidential Address economic strategy, focusing on inflation control, price monitoring, and tax reform. Key measures include a one-month deadline for inflation reduction plans, intensified price oversight, and a proposal for a "wealth tax" within a month. The minimum wage will increase to 110,000 tenge from January 1st.

item.title: Russian Students Involved in Drone and Munitions Production for Army
item.description: Students in at least 40 Russian colleges and universities are reportedly involved in assembling combat drones, munitions components, and other military products within their educational institutions. Investigations reveal students at the Nazarovo Agricultural College are building FPV drones for deployment to eastern Ukraine. Some students participate in programs offering stipends and employment with defense contractors.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Penalties for Casinos and Bookmakers on Money Laundering
item.description: Kazakhstan is planning stricter penalties for casino, bookmaker, and lottery organizers for violations of anti-money laundering laws. The Ministry of Tourism and Sports has prepared a draft order to hold both companies and responsible employees accountable for financial control failures. This includes personal responsibility for non-compliance with procedures.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Orders Overhaul of Investment Attraction System
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov emphasized the need to improve investment attraction and increase its contribution to economic development. He instructed ministries to establish a unified system for managing investment processes within ten days, clarifying responsibilities and centralizing investor relations. Priority will be given to deep processing and labor productivity projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan to pilot new social payment system for high-income citizens
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to integrate its digital family card with banking systems by December 2026, phasing in a new social payment system from January 2027. The pilot project will initially target high-income individuals to assess the effectiveness of new social assistance optimization measures before wider implementation. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection stated that the approach will consider family living conditions.

item.title: Kyrgyz activist demands state compensation; court hearing set for November 10
item.description: Bishkek's Pervomaysky District Court will continue hearing activist Perizat Suranova's claim for state compensation on November 10. Suranova filed the lawsuit on October 7, seeking damages for alleged rights violations. She was among 22 individuals acquitted in the controversial Kempir-Abad case in June 2024, a verdict upheld by the Bishkek City Court in March 2026.

item.title: Salaries for 77,000 medical workers in Kazakhstan to increase by 40% from 2027
item.description: The salaries of 77,000 medical workers in Kazakhstan are set to increase by 40% starting in 2027. This measure aims to improve compensation for healthcare professionals. Further details on the implementation and specific criteria for the increase are expected as the date approaches.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Government and banks to integrate family financial data by December 1
item.description: Government bodies and banks in Kazakhstan must integrate databases on family financial status by December 1 to accurately assess household well-being. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov instructed the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection to ensure system integration. This initiative is part of broader reforms to social policy, with data sharing requiring recipient consent.

item.title: Afghan border regions with Iran and Pakistan become new global drug production centers
item.description: Following the Taliban's widespread ban on illicit drugs in 2022, opium production in Afghanistan has significantly decreased. However, cultivation is increasingly shifting to neighboring Pakistan and Iran. Border regions in Pakistan's Balochistan and Iran's Sistan and Baluchestan provinces are seeing expanded poppy cultivation, becoming new global centers for drug production.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prime Minister Orders Price Controls and Winter Food Stockpiling
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has ordered urgent measures to curb inflation and ensure sufficient food supplies for winter. He instructed government bodies to coordinate fiscal and monetary policies to lower inflation and increase real incomes by November 20. Regional authorities are tasked with weekly price monitoring, and ministries must ensure food reserves are established within two weeks.

item.title: Second Phase of 'Umai' Mortgage Program for Women Launches in Kazakhstan
item.description: The second phase of Kazakhstan's 'Umai' mortgage program for women begins on November 3. The Asian Development Bank has disbursed a second tranche of 20 billion tenge to 'Otbank' for loan issuance. The first tranche of 9 billion tenge has been nearly fully utilized, helping 420 women purchase homes, with another 230 in the process of selecting apartments.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Connect Rural Entrepreneurs to E-commerce Marketplaces
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to expand e-commerce access for rural residents by connecting local entrepreneurs to existing marketplaces. The initiative includes developing pickup points in remote areas and providing training in e-commerce and digital tools. Over 500,000 Kazakhs already earn through digital platforms, with plans to enhance logistics and digital skills training.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Review Teacher Reporting Requirements to Reduce Workload
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister has instructed the Ministry of Education and regional authorities to review all teacher reporting forms. The goal is to reduce non-essential administrative burdens on educators and protect their professional authority. Proposals to enhance the protection of teachers' honor and dignity are due by December 10.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Proposes Higher Taxes for the Wealthy
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has proposed discussing a higher tax rate for individuals with substantial wealth. He emphasized that this aims for a fair contribution to the country's development. The government and Parliament will study the proposal, with details on the new rate yet to be specified.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Orders Stricter Contractor Liability for Poor Road Repairs
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed the Ministry of Transport to develop measures for increasing the accountability of contractors and technical supervisors for the quality of road construction and repair. He emphasized the ministry's responsibility for all road projects and the condition of road surfaces. The directive also includes completing modernization of border crossing points, launching a new railway line, and expanding key highways.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Sets November 20 Deadline for Inflation Reduction Measures
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has set a November 20 deadline for the government to develop and implement measures to curb inflation. The Ministry of National Economy and the National Bank are tasked with coordinating fiscal and monetary policies to lower inflation and increase real incomes. The Ministry of Trade is to strengthen control over price caps on essential food items and prevent unjustified price hikes.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Revise Social Assistance Rules, Considering Property and Income
item.description: Kazakhstan is updating its methodology for assessing family income, property, and obligations when assigning social assistance. The revised approach prioritizes identifying individuals' actual financial situation and need for aid. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection is reviewing how income, credit obligations, and vehicle ownership are evaluated.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Offer 20% Discount and Free Rides for Electronic Transport Tickets
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering introducing discounts and free ride privileges to encourage electronic payments for public transport. A draft presidential decree proposes a minimum 20% discount for electronic tickets on suburban trains and buses from 2027 to 2029. By 2030, cash payments for these routes will be phased out entirely.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Proposes Higher Tax Rate for Wealthy Citizens
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has proposed considering a higher tax rate for citizens with substantial wealth. He instructed the government and Parliament to review the tax policy, emphasizing the need for a fair system. Tokayev noted that while the new Tax Code provides a foundation, some issues require revision to ease business burdens.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Activist Claims Obstruction in Maslikhat Election Candidacy
item.description: Baglan Ziyabekov, an activist and former maslikhat deputy, alleges obstruction in his attempt to register as a candidate for the upcoming local elections in May district, Pavlodar region. He claims he faced resistance, was forcibly taken to a police station, and denied application forms, citing his past efforts to address corruption.

item.title: US Warns Allies to Prepare for Potential Attacks on Iran
item.description: The United States has alerted several Middle Eastern allies to prepare for potential military action against Iran and possible Iranian retaliatory strikes following the US midterm elections. While President Trump has not made a final decision, officials indicated that new military action could last several days, heightening regional alert.

item.title: Kyrgyzstani Boxer Wins Bronze at World Youth Championship
item.description: Meeim Chynybekova from Kyrgyzstan secured a bronze medal at the World Youth Boxing Championship in Montenegro. Competing in the U-19 category, she reached the semi-finals and ultimately placed third after a loss to an Indian opponent.

item.title: Construction Begins on Artificial Lake in Tashkent's Olmazor District
item.description: Construction has commenced on a new park featuring an artificial lake in Tashkent's Olmazor district. The lake will cover 0.5 hectares, with a depth of 2 meters. The project aims to improve the area's appearance and ecological environment.

item.title: North Korea Fires Ballistic Missiles Again, Prompting Japanese Warning and South Korean Alert
item.description: North Korea has launched approximately ten ballistic missiles towards the East Sea, triggering an emergency warning from Japan and placing South Korea on high military alert. The missiles were reportedly fired from the Wonsan area. This launch follows recent tactical ballistic missile tests and a reported successful test of an AI-equipped underwater drone by North Korea.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Chamber of Commerce Criticizes Border Delays with Kazakhstan
item.description: The President of Kyrgyzstan's Chamber of Commerce, Temir Sariev, has voiced concerns over ongoing border delays between Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan, which continue to hinder businesses despite increased trade. He noted that hundreds of Kyrgyz trucks face long queues, leading to spoiled goods and missed deadlines. The delays also negatively impact tourism, particularly for visitors to Issyk-Kul Lake.

item.title: Central Asian Countries Aim to Integrate QR System for Cross-Border Payments
item.description: Central Asian countries and Azerbaijan are working to integrate a QR system to facilitate cross-border payments. A regional meeting in Dushanbe focused on developing payment systems, including instant payment systems and unified QR standards. A joint working group will explore models for integrating national payment infrastructures, particularly for QR-code-based cross-border transactions and ensuring interoperability of instant payment systems.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Ministry Denies Reports of Attack on Opposition Leader Adakhan Madumarov
item.description: The Ministry of Internal Affairs of Kyrgyzstan has refuted claims of an assault on Adakhan Madumarov, leader of the "Butun Kyrgyzstan" party. The ministry urged citizens to rely on official sources and avoid spreading false information. Madumarov has not yet commented on the reports.

item.title: Fourth Central Asia Inter-Parliamentary Forum Opens in Dushanbe
item.description: The Fourth Inter-Parliamentary Forum of Central Asian countries has opened in Dushanbe, Tajikistan. Delegations from Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Kyrgyzstan are attending. The forum, themed "Unity for Peace, Security, and Prosperity of Central Asia," aims to foster regional cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Extending Unemployment Benefits to Four Months
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering extending unemployment benefits from three to four months. Currently, nearly 80,000 individuals receive up to 4 million Uzbek soms in unemployment aid. Beneficiaries are also offered free vocational training and stipends at career centers, according to the Ministry of Employment.

item.title: New Tashkent Designed for People, Not Robots, Says Lead Designer
item.description: Hakan Agja, lead designer for New Tashkent, stated that cities should be designed for people, not robots. He emphasized that New Tashkent aims to be a fully-fledged city with its own life, not just residential and administrative areas. This approach is crucial for planned urban expansion to accommodate projected population growth.

item.title: Central Asian Parliament Heads Visit Tajikistan's National Theater
item.description: Leaders of the parliaments of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and Turkmenistan, along with a parliamentary delegation from Kyrgyzstan, visited Tajikistan's National Theater in Dushanbe. The visit followed their participation in the Fourth Interparliamentary Forum of Central Asian States. Guests toured the theater's facilities and admired its national and modern architectural elements.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Rail Link Between New Tashkent Airport and Northern Station
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to develop rail links connecting major cities' train stations and airports by 2030, including a connection between the new Tashkent airport and the "Tashkent-Severnaya" railway station. The strategy also includes establishing transport hubs and launching a unified digital transport platform by 2028.
